title: Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster
lede: Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia will stop selling H200 chips in China, ending its part in a Trump-brokered exception to US limits on exporting advanced AI chips there.

points: The arrangement, negotiated by Huang, routed chips through the US so the government could collect a 25% tariff.
Nvidia also set up a board committee for national security, export compliance and trade risk.
Rules issued Monday bar advanced US chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely.
Jefferies estimates the rules could take $44 billion to $62 billion off next year's data center revenue; Kress says the backlog means no top-line hit.
China had already refused most H200 deliveries, preferring to build demand for domestic chips.

sections.text: Large training clusters outside China will have to certify they serve no Chinese customers before buying Nvidia chips, which may push some operators toward other accelerators.
